sources.title: Tarkir: Dragonstorm Prerelease Guide: What You Need to Know
sources.author: Jubilee Finnegan

mechanics.name: Endure
mechanics.summary: When a creature endures N, choose either N +1/+1 counters on it or an N/N white Spirit token; if the creature is gone when the ability resolves, you still get the token. This lets Abzan pivot between building tall and going wide.

mechanics.name: Flurry
mechanics.summary: Flurry triggers when you cast your second spell each turn, regardless of what happened to the first spell, and only once per turn. Cheap spells, mana boosts, and recastable effects turn the trigger into Jeskai tempo and pressure.

mechanics.name: Renew
mechanics.summary: Renew abilities exile their card from your graveyard as part of a sorcery-speed activation; every renew effect puts counters on a creature, often +1/+1 or keyword counters, and some add another effect. Self-mill turns fallen creatures into Sultai value while cards leaving the graveyard feed overlap payoffs.

mechanics.name: Mobilize
mechanics.summary: When a creature with mobilize N attacks, it creates N tapped and attacking 1/1 red Warrior tokens, then sacrifices them at the beginning of the next end step. Mardu exploits the temporary bodies with go-wide bonuses, sacrifice outlets, and death triggers.

mechanics.name: Harmonize
mechanics.summary: You may cast a harmonize spell from your graveyard for its harmonize cost, optionally tapping one untapped creature you control to reduce only the generic portion by that creature's power; it is exiled whenever it leaves the stack. Temur turns big creatures into discounted graveyard spells, while the cast also fuels flurry and leaves-the-graveyard triggers.

mechanics.name: Omens + Behold
mechanics.summary: Omen cards may be cast using their instant or sorcery Omen characteristics and shuffle into their owner's library if they resolve; in other zones, only their Dragon creature characteristics apply. To behold a Dragon, choose one you control or reveal a Dragon card from hand, discounting or upgrading several spells.

mechanics.name: Dragons + Dragonstorms
mechanics.summary: The five monocolor Dragonstorm enchantments each have an enters effect and return to their owner's hand whenever a Dragon you control enters, letting you replay that effect. Dragons and Omen cards also turn on behold and reward decks that can support a critical mass.

archetypes.name: Token sacrifice grind
archetypes.playstyle: Build expendable Spirit and Warrior tokens through endure and mobilize, attack wide, then cash temporary bodies into cards or drain before the end-step sacrifice. Efficient white-black removal lets the deck trade aggressively and grind longer than the red-white swarm.

archetypes.name: Mobilize go-wide aggro
archetypes.playstyle: Curve out with cheap mobilize creatures, flood combat with temporary Warriors, and turn width into pings, scaling attackers, or a lethal Frontline Rush. Keep the curve low enough to double-spell for the flurry package, but prioritize bodies and attacks over a fragile spells-only build.

archetypes.name: Two-spell value
archetypes.playstyle: Bank cheap cantrips, mana effects, and harmonize spells to double-spell on demand, turning each second cast into flying tokens, cards, or burst damage. Trade tempo early, then let repeatable flurry value take over the midgame.
keyCards: Marang River Regent // Coil and Catch

archetypes.name: Graveyard recycling value
archetypes.playstyle: Stock the graveyard with selective self-mill, then cash those cards out through renew, harmonize, and recursion to trigger card draw and scaling threats. Cheap interaction buys time for repeated graveyard exchanges to bury the opponent.
keyCards: Marang River Regent // Coil and Catch

archetypes.name: Counters midrange
archetypes.playstyle: Layer endure and renew counters onto resilient attackers, then convert that growth into cards, evasion, and snowballing combat advantages. Trade early, stock the graveyard, and back the largest threat with efficient removal.
